h1: Quebec City travel, stays & events guide
heroText: Quebec City is a Canada base best planned around named sights rather than a generic stopover. Start with Old Quebec, add Chateau Frontenac, and use Petit-Champlain to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Quebec City International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

history.label: 1500s
history.text: French regime (1500s–1763) Quebec City is one of the oldest European settlements in North America and the only fortified city north of Mexico whose walls still exist.

It was then made the capital of Lower Canada by the Constitutional Act of 1791.

history.label: 1800s
history.text: The city experienced an economic golden age in the 1800s, due to its favorable location on the Saint Lawrence River which gave rise to industries of wooden sailing ships manufacture, export of squared timber.
From 1841 to 1867, the capital of the Province of Canada rotated between Kingston, Montreal, Toronto, Ottawa and Quebec City (from 1851 to 1855 and from 1859 to 1865).
In 1867, Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the definite capital of the Dominion of Canada, while Quebec City was confirmed as the capital of the newly created province of Quebec.
Before the Royal Military College of Canada was established in 1876, the only French-speaking officer training school was the Quebec City School of Military Instruction, founded in 1864.
The fort was at the mouth of the Rivière du Cap Rouge, in the suburban former town of Cap-Rouge (which merged into Quebec City in 2002).

history.label: Regional role
history.text: Although the Acadian settlement at Port-Royal was established three years earlier, Quebec came to be known as the cradle of North America's Francophone population.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The town was distinguished by its monumental architecture, fortifications, and affluent homes of masonry and shacks in the suburbs of Saint-Jean and Saint-Roch.
